claim: Scenario annotation create, edit, resolve, and reopen events now receive the same post-commit exact-hash registered-installation attribution in product and MCP paths as scenario votes. Bodies remain in collaborative lifecycle history but are omitted from attestation inspection and mutation responses.
proved: Canonical SHA-256 includes every strict annotation event field, including lifecycle action, nullable body, parent, scenario/turn/annotation/event identities, author/display-name snapshot, and timestamp.

The shared resolver re-reads the exact retained annotation event, recomputes its hash, rejects a mutated retained body, and validates the registered installation/participant claim before accepting the attestation.
Product mutation checks document/project identity before invoking its commit closure; MCP retains and returns the exact event from each revision-guarded mutation before best-effort signing.
Directory, signing, registration, or ledger failure returns explicit unsigned state after commit and never disguises or rolls back the annotation event.
Headless UI contracts expose pending, signed-device, and unsigned states while denying person or organization identity; labels remain independently usable while annotation signing is pending.
Inspection returns bounded event/key/participant/hash/time metadata and omits annotation bodies, display names, public keys, and signatures.
notProved: That a self-issued installation key authenticates a person or organization, prevents Sybil claims, supplies legal consent, or provides trusted time.
Durable attribution for the eight remaining named research-event domains, identity-key rotation/recovery, or append-only survival against a malicious Yjs writer.
Physical packaged two-install product/MCP interaction; current proof is deterministic headless domain, product-copy, mutation-path, and resolver coverage.
